info.title: ManyPI API
info.description: The REST API behind ManyPI — AI lead generation, email validation, cold-email outreach, agent runs and web scraping. Every endpoint is authenticated with a ManyPI API key (`mpi_...`) or an OAuth 2.1 access token, and honours the permissions granted to that credential.

tags.name: Leads
tags.description: Find, store, enrich and manage leads.

tags.name: Email validation
tags.description: Verify that lead addresses can receive mail.

tags.name: Outreach
tags.description: Inboxes, sequences, campaigns, sending and replies.

tags.name: Endpoints
tags.description: Publish scrapers as typed REST endpoints.

get.description:
List and filter the workspace's leads, newest first. Also returns the declared custom columns, the past lead searches that produced these leads, the workspace total and the plan's lead limit — everything a grid needs in one call.

When the workspace is locked for billing, the response keeps the same shape but carries `billingLock`, and `leads` holds placeholder rows rather than real leads. Check for `billingLock` before you store or act on the rows.

Requires the `read` permission.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free text across company, full name, email and domain.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: A lead status, or `archived` / `unsubscribed` (which are flags, not statuses).

parameters.name: campaign
parameters.description: The agent run id of the lead search that produced the leads.

parameters.name: brand
parameters.description: Narrow to one brand, or `all` for the whole workspace.

workspaceTotal.description: Every lead the workspace stores, ignoring filters.

campaigns.description: Past lead searches, with how many leads each produced.

billingLock.description: Present only when the workspace is locked for billing. `leads` then holds placeholder rows and `total` is the number of real leads waiting behind the lock.

patch.description:
Change status and/or archive state for up to 500 leads at once.

Requires the `write` permission.

delete.description:
Permanently delete up to 500 leads. Consider archiving instead — archived leads stop appearing everywhere but stay recoverable.

Requires the `write` permission.

get.description:
Fetch one lead with its custom columns and email status.

Requires the `read` permission.

patch.description:
Update one field, the status, the score, or the archive flag on a single lead. Setting `field` to a name that is not a core field writes into the lead's custom columns.

Requires the `write` permission.

field.description: A core field (`company`, `full_name`, `title`, `email`, `phone`, `domain`, `linkedin_url`, `location`, `source_url`) or a custom column key.

value.description: Empty string or null clears the field.

delete.description:
Permanently delete one lead.

The response is `{ "ok": true }` whether or not a lead with that id existed. To confirm the lead was there, fetch it first with `GET /api/leads/{id}`.

Requires the `write` permission.

post.description:
Launch the lead-generation agent against structured criteria, a saved search, or a set of seed leads ("find more like these").

The run is asynchronous: poll `GET /api/agents/runs` with the returned `conversation_id`. The run may pause with a clarifying question — answer it with `POST /api/agents/runs/{id}/reply` and the same run continues.

`count` is clamped to the workspace's remaining lead capacity; when that happens the response carries a `clamped` block. A full workspace returns `403` with `code: "lead_limit"`.

**With a saved search.** `criteria` sent alongside `profile_id` replaces the saved criteria as a whole — fields you leave out fall back to their defaults, not to the saved values. To change one field, read the saved search from `GET /api/leads/research-profiles`, merge your change, and send the full criteria. Because `save` defaults to `true`, the criteria you send are also written back to that saved search; send `save: false` to run without changing it.

**Two responses that start no lead search.** Both apply only to a typed request, with no `profile_id` and no `seed_lead_ids`:
- When `criteria` carries only a free-text `description` that does not read as a request for leads, ManyPI starts a plain agent run instead and the response includes `redirected: true`. Send `check_intent: false` to skip that check.
- When the description names leads the workspace already has, the response is `{ "known": {...}, "description": "..." }` with no `run_id`, and no run starts. Send `force_search: true` to search anyway.

Requires the `agents` permission.

profile_id.description: Re-run a saved search. Its criteria are used when `criteria` is omitted; when `criteria` is sent, it replaces them entirely.

seed_lead_ids.description: Seed the search from existing leads ("find similar").

save.description: Persist the criteria as a reusable saved search. With `profile_id`, writes them back to that saved search.

check_intent.description: Check that a free-text-only request reads as a lead search, and start a plain agent run when it does not. Send `false` when your integration only ever sends lead searches.

force_search.description: Search even when the description names leads the workspace already has.

criteria.description: E-commerce agencies building Shopify stores for DTC brands

200.description: A run was created — or, when `known` is present instead of `run_id`, the workspace already holds the leads the description names and no run was started.

count.description: Leads the run will actually try to save, after clamping.

clamped.description: Present only when `count` was reduced to fit the plan.

redirected.description: Present and `true` when the request did not read as a lead search and a plain agent run was started instead. See `check_intent`.

known.description: Present instead of `run_id` when the description names leads the workspace already has. Holds those leads; no run was started. See `force_search`.

description.description: The description that was matched, returned alongside `known`.

403.description: The workspace is storing all the leads the plan allows (`code: "lead_limit"`).

get.description:
The workspace's saved lead searches, plus past lead-generation campaigns that were never saved as a profile.

Requires the `read` permission.

post.summary: Create or update a saved search
post.description:
Store a search without running it. Pass `id` to replace an existing profile in place: `criteria` replaces the stored criteria, and an omitted `name` is replaced by one generated from the criteria. To change only some fields — a rename, say — use `PATCH /api/leads/research-profiles/{id}`, which keeps whatever you leave out.

Requires the `write` permission.

patch.description:
Rename a saved search, change its kind, or replace its criteria. Anything you leave out keeps its stored value. `criteria`, when sent, replaces the stored criteria as a whole.

Requires the `write` permission.

delete.description:
Delete a saved search. Leads it already found are kept.

The response is `{ "ok": true }` whether or not a saved search with that id existed.

Requires the `write` permission.

post.description:
Write a batch of leads. **Up to 100 rows per request** — chunk larger files client-side so a big import cannot outlive the request timeout and so progress is real.

`declare_fields` lets the same request that carries the first chunk also declare the custom columns those rows write into. It is idempotent, so resending the declarations with every chunk is harmless.

A full workspace still returns `200` — the rows that fitted were written — with `code: "lead_limit"` in the body.

Requires the `write` permission.

duplicates.description: `merge` fills blanks on the existing lead; `overwrite` lets incoming values win; `skip` leaves it untouched.

skippedNoIdentity.description: No email and no domain-plus-name, so there is nothing to file the row under.

remaining.description: Lead slots left after this batch.

code.description: `lead_limit` when the plan filled up mid-import.

get.description:
Stream the filtered leads as CSV, up to 10,000 rows. Honours the same `status` and `q` filters as the list endpoint. Archived leads are excluded unless you ask for them.

Requires the `read` permission.

How many more leads the workspace can store. Read this before starting a large search or import — it changes every time a run saves a lead.

Requires the `read` permission.

The workspace's declared lead columns, in display order. These are column *definitions*; the values live on each lead's `custom` object.

Requires the `read` permission.

post.description:
Declare a column so leads can carry it. Set `auto_research` and the agent fills it in on future lead searches without you restating it each time.

Requires the `write` permission.

200.description: The column already existed and was returned unchanged.

post.description:
Queue an SMTP mailbox probe for lead addresses, raw addresses, or both. Results are written back onto the leads as `email_status`, `email_provider`, `email_is_role` and `email_validated_at`.

Pass `estimate_only` to price the run without queueing it. You are only charged for probes that actually run — cached results and addresses rejected by the cheap pre-check are free.

Requires the `leads:validate` permission, deliberately separate from `write` so a general-purpose key cannot run up a validation bill.

lead_ids.description: Leads in this workspace whose addresses should be checked.

emails.description: Raw addresses, not tied to a lead.

estimate_only.description: Price the run without queueing it.

200.description: The job was queued, or (with `estimate_only`) priced.

schema.description: Two shapes. A normal call queues a job and returns `job_id`, `total` and `estimate`. An `estimate_only` call queues nothing and returns `estimate` alone — with no `job_id` and no `total` — so test for `job_id` before treating the response as a queued job.

billable.description: Probes that will actually run and be charged.

free.description: Cached results and addresses the cheap pre-check rejected.

402.description: Out of validation credits and overage is off (`code: "validation_credits_exhausted"`).

get.description:
The workspace's recent validation jobs, newest first.

Requires the `read` permission.

One validation job plus its per-address results. Poll this for progress and the final breakdown.

Requires the `read` permission.

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: Set to `false` to omit the per-address results.

get.description:
Every connected sending identity with its health: today's sends versus the warmup-aware cap, 14-day delivered/failed/opened/bounced, a rolling 24-hour bounce rate, whether the bounce guard has paused it, and a 0–100 health score.

Use an inbox `id` as `smtp_config_id` when creating a campaign or sending.

Requires the `read` permission.

parameters.name: brand
parameters.description: `all` reports every inbox in the workspace.

get.description:
Saved email sequences with their inline steps. Brand-scoped; `?brand=all` widens to the whole workspace.

Requires the `read` permission.

post.description:
Create the email steps a campaign sends. Step 0 goes out on enrollment; each later step waits `wait_days` after the previous one and, with `thread_mode: "reply"`, threads under the first email. Merge variables: `{{first_name}}`, `{{company}}`, `{{title}}`, `{{domain}}`, `{{location}}`. Bodies are simple HTML — `

`, `
`, ``, ``. A/B variants inside a step require Pro or Business. Requires the `write` permission.

403.description: A/B variants require Pro or Business.

post.description:
AI-draft a cold email (`mode: "email"`) or a whole follow-up sequence (`mode: "sequence"`) from a plain-language brief, written against your brand context.

This only drafts: nothing is saved and nothing is sent. Feed the result into `POST /api/outreach/sequences` or `POST /api/outreach/send`.

Requires the `read` permission.

lead_id.description: An example lead to tailor the tone toward.

example.instructions: We help e-commerce agencies find new client leads without cold-calling. Ask for a 15-minute call.

get.description:
Campaigns with per-campaign stats — enrolled, active, completed, sent, opened, replied — plus the sequence and inbox each is bound to.

Requires the `read` permission.

post.description:
Bind a sequence to a sending inbox. After creating it, enroll leads with `POST /api/outreach/enroll`.

Requires the `write` permission.

daily_limit.description: Never exceeds the inbox's own cap.

priority.description: Higher wins the next paced slot when campaigns share an inbox.

patch.description:
Pause, resume or archive a campaign, or change its name, reply-to, daily limit, schedule or priority. Pausing stops further sends without losing progress.

Requires the `write` permission.

delete.description:
Delete a campaign. Archiving (`PATCH` with `status: "archived"`) is usually the better choice — it keeps the history.

The campaign's sequence is deleted with it when no other campaign uses that sequence.

The response is `{ "ok": true }` whether or not a campaign with that id existed. To confirm it was there, fetch it first with `GET /api/outreach/campaigns/{id}`.

Requires the `write` permission.

200.description: Deleted, or there was nothing to delete.

get.description:
One campaign's full analytics: headline stats, a per-step sent/opened breakdown, and every enrolled lead with its progress.

The per-step breakdown is where you see whether the follow-ups are doing the work.

Requires the `read` permission.

campaign.description: The campaign, with an added `inboxes` array describing the sending identities it uses.

perStep.description: Per-step sent and opened breakdown. Named `perStep`, not `steps`.

leads.description: The enrolled leads with their progress. Named `leads`, not `enrollments`.

post.description:
Queue the campaign's sequence for real sending, respecting the inbox's warmup and daily caps. Up to 1,000 leads per call; ids past the first 1,000 are counted in `skipped_over_limit`.

Skipped rather than failed: leads with no email, leads already enrolled, unsubscribed or suppressed addresses, addresses that bounced, addresses known to be undeliverable, and — when the brand only writes to confirmed addresses — addresses that could not be confirmed. Each cause has its own counter; `summary` explains them in plain language.

When the brand has *validate on enroll* turned on (the default), unchecked addresses are enrolled and checked in the background (`queued_for_validation`). The result is applied at send time, so an address that turns out undeliverable is never sent to.

**Sending cannot be undone.** Requires a paid plan and the `outreach:send` permission.

schema.description: Skips are reported as one counter per cause rather than a single total. Counters for causes that did not occur may be omitted. For the number of leads that were not enrolled, add up every `skipped_*` counter and `already_enrolled` — or compute `requested - enrolled`.

enrolled.description: Leads that now have an enrollment they did not have before. Includes `queued_for_validation`.

requested.description: Lead ids in the request, before any skipping.

already_enrolled.description: Leads already enrolled in this campaign.

skipped_not_found.description: Ids that match no lead this workspace can see.

skipped_unsubscribed.description: Leads who unsubscribed or are on the do-not-contact list.

skipped_bounced.description: Leads whose address bounced the last time you wrote.

skipped_invalid.description: Addresses known to be dead: invalid, disposable, or a domain that takes no mail.

skipped_unverifiable.description: Addresses the mail server would not confirm, skipped because the brand only writes to confirmed addresses.

skipped_over_limit.description: Ids past the first 1,000 in this request.

queued_for_validation.description: Enrolled leads whose unchecked address is being verified in the background, when the brand has validate-on-enroll turned on.

summary.description: What happened, in plain language — the same text the dashboard shows.

example.summary: Added 214 of 240 leads. 9 leads are already in this campaign. 12 leads have no email address yet, so there is nothing to send to. Find their address first, then add them again. 3 leads unsubscribed, so they stay on your do-not-contact list. Remove them from Suppressions if that was a mistake. 2 leads bounced the last time you wrote. Sending again would only damage the reputation of the inbox you send from.

403.description: Outreach requires a paid plan (`code: "outreach_locked"`), or the workspace is over its seat count.

delete.description:
Cancel remaining steps for the given leads. Emails already sent cannot be recalled.

Requires the `outreach:send` permission.

removed.description: Enrollments cancelled. Can be lower than the number of leads supplied — a lead that already finished the sequence has nothing left to cancel.

post.description:
Send a single email to a lead now, outside any sequence. Merge variables are rendered against the lead, the inbox's daily/warmup cap is respected, and the lead is marked `contacted`.

**Cannot be undone.** Requires a paid plan and the `outreach:send` permission.

lead_id.description: Used for merge variables and as the default recipient.

to.description: Explicit recipient; defaults to the lead's address.

cc.description: Copy recipients. `to`, `cc` and `bcc` together may hold at most 10 addresses.

bcc.description: Blind-copy recipients, counted in the same 10-address limit.

429.description: A sending limit is spent: the inbox has sent its warmup-aware cap for the last 24 hours, or the workspace has reached its plan's monthly outreach allowance. `error` says which. Retrying immediately will not succeed — wait for the window to reset or raise the limit.

get.description:
Workspace-wide sending activity: 14 days of sends (sent, failed, opened per day), replies per day, unsubscribes, bounces, active enrollments, and today's sent versus the combined warmup-aware cap.

Requires the `read` permission.

bounced.description: Bucketed by send date, not bounce date, so the figure lines up with the batch that caused it.

unsubRate14d.description: Percentage rounded to a whole number: `4` means 4%.

bounceRate14d.description: Percentage to one decimal place: `9.2` means 9.2%.

sent24h.description: Sends in the last rolling 24 hours, which is the window `capToday` applies to.

capToday.description: Warmup-aware caps summed across every connected inbox.

get.description:
Everything that came back from your campaigns — human replies, auto-replies and bounces — with counts for filter chips and a sentiment summary.

Reading replies requires any paid plan. The **sentiment fields** (`sentiment`, `sentiment_score`, `intent`, `summary`, `analyzed_at`) require Pro or Business and are stripped from the response on other plans.

On those other plans the `sentiment` filter is **ignored, not rejected**: every reply comes back, and the response says `canSeeSentiment: false`. Check that flag before treating the results as filtered — otherwise, say, every reply gets routed as positive.

Requires the `read` permission.

parameters.name: sentiment
parameters.description: Applied only when the plan includes reply intelligence (`canSeeSentiment: true`); ignored otherwise.

canSeeSentiment.description: Whether the plan includes reply intelligence. When `false`, the sentiment fields are stripped and the `sentiment` filter was not applied.

get.description:
What one campaign's replies add up to: how many were real answers rather than bounces or auto-replies, how they read, and concrete, approvable suggestions for what to change.

`campaign` is required. The reply mix is available on every plan; the `sentiment` breakdown needs reply intelligence (Pro or Business), which the response reports as `canUseAi`.

Requires the `read` permission.

parameters.name: campaign
parameters.description: The campaign whose replies to analyse.

suggestions.description: Suggested changes, newest first, up to 50.

payload.description: The exact change applying the suggestion would make.

mix.description: Responses by kind. `reply` is the only one a person wrote.

sentiment.description: Human replies by sentiment. Empty unless `canUseAi` is `true`.

lastReplyAt.description: When the most recent response of any kind arrived.

canUseAi.description: Whether the plan includes reply intelligence.

get.description:
The workspace's do-not-contact list. Nothing on it is ever sent to, by any campaign, from any inbox, in any brand.

Pass `format=csv` to download the whole list.

Requires the `read` permission.

post.description:
Add addresses to the do-not-contact list. Import your existing list on day one — customers, competitors, anyone who has already asked you to stop.

Up to 5,000 addresses per call. Addresses past the first 5,000 are dropped without an error, so split larger lists across calls.

Requires the `write` permission.

added.description: Addresses submitted. Re-adding one already on the list is a no-op and still counts here.

delete.description:
Remove one address from the list. This only clears the block — it does not re-enroll anyone, so a mistaken removal cannot by itself restart emails to someone who opted out.

The response is `{ "ok": true }` whether or not the address was on the list. To know whether it was, search for it first with `GET /api/outreach/suppressions?q=`.

Requires the `write` permission.

post.description:
Start an agent run on a natural-language goal. Asynchronous — poll `GET /api/agents/runs/{id}` for status and results.

A run that hits an ambiguity **pauses** and asks a question rather than guessing; read it from `result_summary` and answer with `POST /api/agents/runs/{id}/reply` to resume the same run.

Requires the `agents` permission.

goal.description: What you want ManyPI to do, in plain language.

output_schema.description: A JSON schema the result must conform to.

example.goal: Find the pricing pages of the ten largest Shopify agencies in Berlin and summarise their packages.

403.description: Too many runs already in flight for the plan.

get.description:
Your recent runs, newest first, narrowed to the workspace and brand you are working in.

Requires the `read` permission.

Full status for one run, plus its artifacts with signed download URLs valid for one hour.

When `status` is `paused`, the agent's question is in `result_summary`.

Requires the `read` permission.

delete.description:
Delete a run along with its events and artifacts.

The response is `{ "ok": true }` whether or not a run with that id existed. To confirm it was there, fetch it first with `GET /api/agents/runs/{id}`.

Requires the `write` permission.

200.description: Deleted, or there was nothing to delete.

post.description:
Deliver a message into a run.

- **Paused run** — the reply is submitted as the answer to the agent's pending question and the *same* run continues mid-thought.
- **Finished run** (`completed` / `failed` / `cancelled`) — a follow-up run starts in the same conversation, inheriting its context and playbook, so "find 25 more like those" keeps saving leads.
- **Still working** — `409`, unless you pass `interrupt: true`, which cancels it and starts a new run with your message.

Requires the `agents` permission.

interrupt.description: Stop a still-working run, then start a new one with this message.

example.message: Only agencies with a team page and at least five people.

409.description: The run is still working. Wait for it to pause or finish, cancel it, or pass `interrupt: true`.

post.description:
Stop a run immediately. Cancellation is authoritative rather than advisory — a `queued`, `planning` or `running` run is marked `cancelled` at once, so a wedged executor cannot keep it "running" and occupying one of your parallel-run slots. A `paused` run is cancelled through its cancel flag.

Runs that already finished (`completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`) are left as they are. The response is `{ "ok": true }` in every case, including for an id that matches no run — read the run with `GET /api/agents/runs/{id}` to see its status.

Requires the `agents` permission.

200.description: Cancelled, or there was nothing to cancel.

get.description:
Skills available to the caller: ManyPI's premade ones plus the workspace's own.

Requires the `read` permission.

200.description: Skills, as a bare array rather than an object wrapper.

post.description:
Create a custom skill — a reusable instruction set injected into the agent's system prompt for a run.

Instructions shape behaviour but never widen tool access: custom skills are always created with the safe defaults.

Requires the `write` permission.

example.title: Company research
example.system_prompt: For the company given, research what they sell, who their customers are, recent funding or hiring news, and the two people most likely to own the buying decision. Cite a source URL for every fact.

get.description:
The workspace's scrapers with their schema, target URL, status and type.

Requires the `read` permission.

post.description:
Queue a scraper run. **Asynchronous** — the call returns `202` immediately with a `runId`, so a slow page never times your request out.

Poll `GET /api/runs/{runId}` until `status` is `completed` (or `failed`), then read the full result with `GET /api/{scraperId}/data/{runId}`. Or configure an outbound webhook to be notified when it completes.

The body takes `url` only. Run settings such as timeouts and retries are not configurable per call.

Requires the `scraper` permission.

parameters.name: scraperId
parameters.description: Find this in the dashboard under Scrapers.

url.description: Override the scraper's saved target for this run.

404.description: No such scraper for this account.

get.description:
The extracted data for one run. It carries no status: until the run completes, the body is `null`. Check progress with `GET /api/runs/{runId}` and call this once `status` is `completed`.

Requires the `read` permission.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: A run id. Also accepts `latest` for the scraper's most recent run, a number for the run that many places back (`1` is the one before `latest`), or the run's exact `created_at` timestamp.

200.description: The extracted data itself, or `null` while the run has not completed. This endpoint returns the scraped JSON directly — there is no run envelope, so no id, status, error or timestamp is included. The shape follows the scraper's own `scraper_schema`. Large results are hydrated from storage transparently, so the full result is always returned rather than a truncated preview.

schema.description: Matches the scraper's configured output schema.

get.description:
Recent scraper runs across every scraper, with status and extracted data. Returned as a flat array, which is the shape polling-based integrations such as Zapier expect for a trigger.

Requires the `read` permission.

The status of one scraper run — the call to poll after `POST /api/scrape/{scraperId}`.

`result` holds the inline copy of the extracted data once the run completes. Large results keep only a preview inline, so read the full data from `GET /api/{scraperId}/data/{runId}`.

Requires the `read` permission.

result.description: Present once `status` is `completed`. May be a preview for large results.

downloadUrl.description: Storage path of the full result, when one was written.

403.description: The run belongs to another account.

get.description:
Your published endpoints and the scrapers backing them.

Requires the `read` permission.

post.description:
Publish a scraper as a typed REST endpoint at `https://app.manypi.com/v1/e/{slug}`.

Slugs are unique per account and resolve within the key owner's endpoints, so your slug namespace is your own.

Requires the `write` permission.

param_schema.description: JSON Schema for the input. Validated on every call.

403.description: Endpoint limit reached for the plan.

409.description: That slug is already in use.

get.description:
One endpoint's settings and its 50 most recent invocations.

Requires the `read` permission.

patch.description:
Change an endpoint's settings, or take it offline with `is_active: false`. The slug and the backing scraper cannot be changed — create a new endpoint for that.

Requires the `write` permission.

is_active.description: `false` takes the endpoint offline: calls to its URL return `404` until it is turned back on.

delete.description:
Delete an endpoint permanently. Its URL stops answering at once.

The response is `{ "ok": true }` whether or not an endpoint with that id existed.

Requires the `write` permission.

200.description: Deleted, or there was nothing to delete.

get.description:
Call one of your published endpoints, passing its parameters in the query string. Query values arrive as strings and are converted to the types the endpoint's `param_schema` declares. To send typed values or nested objects, use `POST` with a JSON body instead — it works whatever method the endpoint was created with.

How a call resolves: a fresh cached result is returned immediately (no crawl credits spent; `X-ManyPI-Cache: hit`); otherwise the scrape runs inline, up to a ~110 second budget; if it exceeds that — or the endpoint is `async` — you get `202` with a run id to poll at `GET /v1/e/{slug}/results/{runId}`.

Requires the `endpoints:invoke` permission.

400.description: Parameters failed validation against the endpoint's schema. `details` lists what was wrong.

404.description: No active endpoint with that slug for this account.

post.summary: Invoke an endpoint with a JSON body
post.description:
Call one of your published endpoints with its parameters as a JSON object. Values keep their JSON types, so numbers, booleans and nested objects arrive as sent. Works for every endpoint, whichever method it was created with.

Resolves exactly like `GET`: a fresh cached result immediately, otherwise the scrape runs inline for up to ~110 seconds, then `202` with a run id.

Requires the `endpoints:invoke` permission.

schema.description: The endpoint's parameters, validated against its `param_schema`.

400.description: Parameters failed validation against the endpoint's schema. `details` lists what was wrong.

404.description: No active endpoint with that slug for this account.

get.description:
Collect the result of a call that returned `202` — an `async` endpoint, or a sync one that ran past the inline budget. Returns `202` again while the run is still going.

Requires the `endpoints:invoke` permission.

404.description: No endpoint with that slug, or no such run, for this account.

get.summary: Validate a key / get account info
get.description: The cheapest way to confirm a key works. Returns the owning user, the key's permissions and its rate limit.

bearerAuth.description: A ManyPI API key (`mpi_...`) from the profile menu → API Access in the dashboard, or an OAuth 2.1 access token obtained through the MCP consent flow.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid or expired credential — or a key that lacks the permission this route requires.

BadRequest.description: The request body or parameters failed validation.

NotFound.description: No such resource in this workspace.

EndpointResult.description: The extracted data, matching the endpoint's output schema. `X-ManyPI-Cache` says whether it came from the cache (`hit`) or a fresh scrape (`miss`); `X-ManyPI-Run-Id` names the run behind it.

X-ManyPI-Cached-At.description: When the cached result was produced. Sent on cache hits only.

EndpointAccepted.description: Still running — the endpoint is `async`, or the scrape ran past the ~110 second inline budget. Poll the URL in `poll` (also sent as `Location`) with `GET /v1/e/{slug}/results/{runId}`.

poll.description: Path of the result to poll, e.g. `/v1/e/{slug}/results/{runId}`.

EndpointFailed.description: The scrape failed (`error: "Scrape failed"`), or it finished but the result did not match the endpoint's output schema. In the second case `details` lists the mismatches and `raw` carries the result that was produced — the credits for it are already spent.

error.description: Human-readable message. A few validation failures (creating or updating an endpoint, bulk lead updates and deletes) send a list of the individual problems here instead of one string.

code.description: A machine-readable code on gated failures: `lead_limit`, `outreach_locked`, `validation_credits_exhausted`.

details.description: Extra detail on some failures, such as the list of parameters that failed an endpoint's `param_schema`.

custom.description: Values for the workspace's declared custom columns.

agent_run_id.description: The lead search that produced this lead.

auto_research.description: The agent fills this in on future lead searches.

key.description: Derived from the label when absent.

ImportRow.description: A lead needs an email, or a domain plus a name, or it cannot be filed and is skipped.

custom.description: Keys must match declared columns, or the values are dropped.

LeadResearchCriteria.description: The structured search. The description does most of the work; the rest is what the agent enforces.

count.description: How many NEW leads to save. Clamped to remaining plan capacity.

company_size.description: Free text on purpose: "5-50 employees", "Series A", "under $5M ARR".

titles.description: Roles to reach inside each company.

exclusions.description: Hard excludes — matches are dropped, not saved.

required_fields.description: A lead missing one of these is not saved.

extra_columns.description: Extra researched columns, written to the lead's custom fields.

sources.description: Where to look: directories, marketplaces, maps, specific sites.

counts.description: How many addresses landed in each status.

name.description: The inbox label, which is often the address itself.

from.description: The sending address. Falls back to the SMTP username when no from-address is set.

sent24h.description: Sends in the last rolling 24 hours — the window `cap` applies to.

cap.description: Warmup-aware cap for the current window, not the raw daily limit.

dailyLimit.description: The inbox's configured daily limit, before warmup is applied.

bounceRate14d.description: Percentage to one decimal place: `9.2` means 9.2%.

warmingUp.description: True while the inbox is still ramping and `cap` is below `dailyLimit`.

sendingPausedAt.description: Set when the bounce guard paused the inbox.

health.description: Delivery success rate, capped at 94 while warming up and reduced four points per percent of 14-day bounce rate.

subject.description: Merge variables allowed. Empty on a `reply` step, which sends as "Re:" the first email's subject.

wait_days.description: Days after the previous step. Step 0 is 0.

send_days.description: Weekdays to send on, as `Date.getDay()` numbers: 0 is Sunday, 1 is Monday, 6 is Saturday. Values outside 0-6 are discarded, so an ISO-style Sunday of 7 is dropped rather than honoured. Defaults to `[1,2,3,4,5]` when omitted, or when every supplied value is discarded.

inbox_strategy.description: How sends are spread when several inboxes are available.

include_unsubscribe.description: Whether an unsubscribe link is appended to each email.

require_verified.description: Whether unverified addresses are validated before enrollment.

unsubscribed_sends.description: Sends that went to an address which later opted out.

sentiment.description: Pro and Business only; stripped from the response on other plans.

result_summary.description: The result — or, while `paused`, the agent's question to you.

download_url.description: Signed URL, valid for one hour.

scraper_schema.description: The JSON Schema the extracted data conforms to.

ScraperRun.description: A scraper run as returned by `GET /api/runs`. The extracted data is also spread onto the root of each run, so a completed run carries that scraper's own fields alongside the ones below; the fields here win on a name collision.

result.description: The extracted data. Null until the run completes.

downloadUrl.description: Storage path for the full JSON result.
